es.meta.title: camsync: graba video vertical con tu iPhone y contrólalo desde tu Mac
es.meta.description: camsync es un estudio de captura en el navegador: el iPhone graba en calidad completa y la Mac controla la toma y recibe el original por la red local.
es.intro.title: Graba video vertical con tu iPhone y contrólalo desde tu Mac
es.intro.lede: camsync es un estudio de captura y producción de video vertical que funciona en el navegador. El iPhone abre una página que usa su cámara, manda una vista en vivo a un panel de control en la Mac por la red local y graba el original en calidad completa, que se va subiendo a la Mac en partes de un segundo.
es.intro.status: Hoy es un prototipo que funciona. Abajo está lo que medimos, lo que hace y lo que todavía no existe.
es.today.title: Qué hace hoy
es.today.live: Vista en vivo del iPhone en el panel de control de la Mac.
es.today.master: Grabación del original en el iPhone, en calidad completa, que se sube a la Mac en partes de un segundo mientras grabas.
es.today.control: Desde la Mac inicias y detienes la grabación y eliges la resolución, la forma (16:9 o 4:3), el lente y el zoom.
es.today.local: El video viaja por tu red local entre el iPhone y la Mac; no pasa por un servidor de MADFAM.

en.meta.title: camsync: record vertical video on your iPhone and control it from your Mac
en.meta.description: camsync is a browser-based capture studio: the iPhone records at full quality while the Mac controls the take and receives the master over the local network.
en.intro.title: Record vertical video on your iPhone and control it from your Mac
en.intro.lede: camsync is a vertical-video capture and production studio that runs in the browser. The iPhone opens a web page that uses its camera, sends a live view to a control panel on the Mac over the local network, and records the full-quality master, which is uploaded to the Mac in one-second chunks.
en.intro.status: Today it is a working prototype. Below is what we measured, what it does and what does not exist yet.
en.today.title: What it does today
en.today.live: A live view of the iPhone in the control panel on the Mac.
en.today.master: The full-quality master is recorded on the iPhone and uploaded to the Mac in one-second chunks while you record.
en.today.control: From the Mac you start and stop recording and choose the resolution, the shape (16:9 or 4:3), the lens and the zoom.
en.today.local: The video travels over your local network between the iPhone and the Mac; it does not go through a MADFAM server.
en.measured.title: What we measured
en.measured.intro: Measured on 24 November 2026 with an iPhone 15.
en.measured.caption: Measured resolution and frames per second
en.measured.format: Masters are MP4 files with H.264 video and AAC audio.
en.measured.remote: Starting and stopping the recording from the Mac works.
en.measured.limit: We have measured it with that iPhone only. We do not yet know how it behaves on other models.
en.notyet.title: What does not exist yet
en.notyet.intro: None of this is built. If you need it today, camsync does not have it.
en.notyet.titles: Titles and graphics over the video.
en.notyet.log: An event log of the take.
en.notyet.app: A native app: today everything runs in the browser.
en.use.title: How it is used today
en.use.1: Connect the Mac and the iPhone to the same local network.
en.use.2: On the Mac, from the project folder, start the studio:
en.use.3: Open the control panel on the Mac. It shows the address to open in Safari on the iPhone.
en.use.4: On the iPhone, allow the camera and the microphone. From the Mac you start and stop the take; the master is saved to a folder on the Mac.
en.use.cert: The first time, Safari warns that the Mac's certificate is self-signed. The Mac creates it when it starts, and it only works inside your local network.
en.use.source: The code is not published yet. Today the studio runs only on your local network; it is not served from the internet.
en.foot.quiet: This page uses no cookies and no analytics, and it does not appear in search engines.
